column1: # TAINT CLOSURE -- every lemma that transitively APPLIES one of the cone's two admits.
# Generated by tools/taint_closure.py; enforced by cert_gate_split.sh PHASE 5.
# BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE FATAL: a lemma ENTERING this closure means an admit reached
# further than it did; a lemma LEAVING it means the containment argument changed.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.  The gate pinned the admits' STATEMENTS but never checked HOW FAR
# THEY REACH.  README asserts "neither admit reaches the headline"; until 2026-08-25 that
# was a hand-verified claim re-checked by hand each time.  It is now gate-enforced.
# The memory note this closes recorded the exact fail-open: "`ledger class = 0` computed
# file-locally reads as 'admit-free cone' -- assert instead that the file never APPLIES
# the tainted lemma."
# THE TWO CHAINS, and note that BOTH TERMINATE IN A DEAD LEAF:
#   A  nhchwcoll_hchwpre_msg (ADMIT, and REFUTABLE -- a collision falsifies the whole
#      five-hypothesis lemma)
#        -> Step_Game4_WOTSTWES_SMDTPREC        (WOTS_TW_ES.ec:6542)
#        -> MEUFGCMA_WOTSTWESNPRF
#        -> EUFNAGCMA_FLSLXMSSMTTWCESNPRF_Unfolded   <-- APPLIED BY NOTHING
#   B  extract_op (ADMIT)
#        -> fors_c_tree_port                     <-- APPLIED BY NOTHING
#            (FORS_C_TreePort.ec is a certification ROOT; nothing `require`s it)
# WIRING `_Unfolded` INTO THE HEADLINE IS THE NAMED REGRESSION this file guards against:
# it would promote a REFUTABLE lemma into the certified result.  PHASE 5 fails on it.
# LABELS.  `sure` = the positional rule decided it.  `ambig` = an `op` of the SAME NAME is
# also in scope, so a name-level tool cannot tell "applies the lemma" from "uses the op".
# The one `ambig` row was resolved BY HAND on 2026-08-25 and IS a genuine lemma
# application: FORS_C_TreePort.ec:1674 reads
#     apply (extract_op A &m struct nd bs los oreg simfid)
# -- adversary and memory arguments, i.e. the lemma (:1485), not the op (:1148).
# The label stays `ambig` because that is what the TOOL can justify; this comment is what
# a HUMAN verified.  Do not "fix" the label to make them agree.
# NOT COVERED (read tools/taint_closure.py's header): a bare `smt()` taking a lemma from
# ambient context without naming it, and reachability via a clone or module argument.
# This is a NAME-LEVEL check, not a proof-term dependency check -- and NOT uniformly safe:
# an exclusion claim needs an OVER-approximation, while both remaining holes SHRINK the
# closure.  Corrected 2026-08-27 (Kimi K3); this header previously said "over-approximation".
